No dual listing exists for a parity check; cross-check: the FY2025 final dividend of HK$0.19 plus the H1-2026 interim of HK$0.12 per share equal roughly RMB0.26/share, consistent with the RMB548.7m of dividends paid in FY2025 on 1,430.6m shares (RMB0.38, which also included the FY2024 final). refresh_price.py moves current_price but never this rate; re-derive fx_rate on any later refresh.

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,430,642,000 shares in issue per the 2026 interim report; basic = diluted because the only potential shares (22.8m options at HK$18.376) are anti-dilutive at the current price. Held FLAT: SBC is negligible and fully expensed; no buyback programme (buyback_cash 0 since FY2023).
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet. total_debt = bank and other borrowings RMB50.0m + lease liabilities RMB273.0m (24.8 current + 248.2 non-current). cash = cash and cash equivalents RMB1,118.6m; restricted cash RMB51.1m EXCLUDED (guarantee deposits). FVTPL wealth-management products (RMB404.0m current + 2.0m non-current) are carried separately in equity_bridge so the reader can see them; their fair-value gains sit in 'other income and gains' and are not in the EBITDA margin path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% risk-free, 7% equity risk premium for mainland-China-exposed HK small caps (country risk included), beta ~1.3 for a connected-party-dependent property-services platform -> cost of equity ~10.9%, rounded to 11%. Debt is RMB50m against RMB1.1bn of cash, so WACC = cost of equity. The same 11% is used in all three scenarios; connected-party, China-property and pivot risk is charged in the flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities (RMB273.0m at 30 Jun 2026) are deducted once in net debt; no lease principal or interest is deducted from the flows (FY2025 cash lease cost was only RMB15m: 12.2m principal + 2.7m interest, because most leased properties are sub-let under the light-asset asset-operation model and carried as investment property at fair value, so ROU assets are only RMB46m). EBITDA is therefore post-IFRS-16. Lease-asset renewal is proxied by lifting the capex path above the 0.7% FY2025 actual.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: NCI book value RMB134.3m (30 Jun 2026) deducted via equity_bridge; the flows are modelled on a consolidated basis. NCI share of profit is ~3% (FY2025 RMB16.4m of RMB575.7m), so the alternative leakage-rate treatment would move value by well under RMB0.05/share.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, on the POST-SPINOFF continuing business only. Midea Real Estate distributed its entire property development and sales business to shareholders on 22 Oct 2024 (Midea Construction (BVI) Ltd; HK$5.90 cash alternative), so FY2016-FY2023 and H1 FY2024 figures (RMB73.6bn revenue, RMB201.6bn assets) describe a different company and are used for nothing here except the historical table. FY0 is FY2025 (Dec year-end), the first full clean year; FY2024 continuing revenue RMB3,725.8m and H1 2026 (RMB1,882.5m, -5.7% YoY) are the other two reference points. What remains is a light-asset services platform: property management ~46% of FY2025 revenue (17% operating margin), asset operation ~20% (37%, lumpy on industrial-park factory deliveries recognised at a point in time), project/development management ~23% (31% in FY2025, 22% in H1 2026, revenue -35% YoY as the controlling shareholder's private development pipeline shrinks), real estate technology ~11% (loss-making, -72% YoY in H1 2026). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, non-US -> owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file (currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset, SBC-zero, charge-risk-once all applied). FY0 CALIBRATION: FY2025 reported EBITDA (operating profit 829.9 + D&A 86.0 = 915.9m, 22.1%) includes a RMB39.8m investment-property fair-value loss and a RMB61.7m PPE/intangible impairment; ex those the underlying margin is 24.5%, and H1 2026 was 23.9% on the same basis. FY0 EBIT x (1-31%) = RMB573m ties to reported total net income RMB575.7m. FY2025 reported FCF RMB947m carried ~RMB180m of working-capital inflow (cash from operations 1,163m vs ~980m of EBITDA plus non-cash charges) that the component build does not repeat: year-1 base owner FCF is ~RMB540m (14% of revenue), deliberately below the 22% FY2025 reported margin. SBC-ZERO: SBC RMB0.3m, so house and street coincide and band_position is null. CASH TAX: TTM cash taxes paid (H2 2025 + H1 2026) RMB266m on TTM PBT RMB851m = 31%; FY2025 P&L effective rate 32.3% (25% PRC CIT plus withholding tax on PRC dividends and non-deductible items); 31% is used flat. MARKET CONTEXT, for the reader: at the current price the stock trades at ~4.8x FY2025 attributable EPS (RMB0.39 = HK$0.46) and yields ~14% on the HK$0.31 of dividends declared for FY2025-H1 2026; the market is pricing the connected-party dependency and the China property cycle far more harshly than an 11% CNY discount rate does, which is why even the bear case sits above the price.
inputs.dividend_note: FY2025 dividends paid RMB548.7m (~98% of attributable profit); interim HK$0.12 (H1 2026) + final HK$0.19 (FY2025). The company is distributing essentially all of its earnings; the model values the flows, not the payout, but a near-100% payout on a shrinking cash pile (RMB1,601m -> RMB1,119m in six months, partly RMB582m of net borrowing repayment) is the practical constraint on the bear case.

2026 interim balance sheet; flows modelled consolidated, NCI charged once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-path 10-year average on the post-spinoff continuing business: FY2024 -> FY2025 revenue +11.4%, H1 2026 -5.7% YoY; project management and real-estate technology shrinking against property-management and asset-operation growth nets to roughly flat near term and ~2.5-3% later.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Multi-year CAGRs are deliberately NOT computed: every pre-FY2024 period includes the property-development business distributed to shareholders in Oct 2024 (revenue RMB73.6bn FY2023 vs RMB3.7bn FY2024 continuing; equity RMB25.3bn vs RMB4.9bn). A 3- or 5-year CAGR across that break is a measure of the spinoff, not of the business being valued. Only two clean annual points exist (FY2024 continuing, FY2025).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history on the continuing basis: FY2025 RMB918.5m (reported 947.1 less SBC 0.3 less interest income 28.3), FY2024 continuing not separable (reported FCF -2,368m is dominated by the discontinued developer's final ten months). H1 2026 owner FCF RMB256m (OCF 278.3 - capex 21.4 - interest income 0.9) vs H1 2025 RMB406m.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -7%: H1 was -5.7% and H2 loses the lumpy H1 industrial-park factory deliveries (RMB314m recognised at a point in time) while project management keeps falling. FY2027 -2% as project management shrinks toward a floor; from FY2028 property management (managed GFA ~84m sqm, growing) and asset operation carry the group to ~3%, fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: 23% in FY2026 is below the 24% underlying of FY2025/H1 2026 because the asset-operation mix normalises after the factory deliveries and real-estate technology stays loss-making; 22.5% thereafter as high-margin project management (31%) shrinks within the mix and property management (17%) grows.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 PPE+intangibles capex was 0.7% of revenue; 1.0% adds a lease-renewal proxy under treatment (A). Investment-property additions were nil in FY2025 investing cash flow.
base.wc_rationale: Negative-working-capital services business (contract liabilities RMB816m, payables RMB2.2bn vs receivables RMB1.1bn): a +10% capture on the revenue CHANGE means revenue declines consume cash in FY2026-27 and growth releases a little later.

bull.growth_rationale: Third-party project-management and non-residential property-management wins (hospitals, elderly care, industrial parks) offset the shrinking connected-party pipeline from FY2027; asset operation scales with new light-asset parks; REMAC ASPACE's Hong Kong MiC pivot stops the losses.
bull.margin_rationale: Underlying 24-24.5% holds in FY2026-27 and rises to 25.5% as real-estate technology reaches breakeven and the flagship mall's 74% NOI margin spreads across a maturing asset-operation portfolio.
bull.capex_rationale: 1.5% funds the asset-operation and third-party expansion.

bear.growth_rationale: The controlling shareholder's development pipeline keeps shrinking (project management -35% YoY in H1 2026 becomes -40%/yr), real-estate technology is wound down, factory deliveries do not recur, and the connected-transaction framework agreements expiring Dec 2026 are renewed on thinner terms. Revenue bottoms ~28% below FY2025 and grows ~1% thereafter.
bear.margin_rationale: Mix shifts entirely to 17%-margin property management plus mall rental; the 31%-margin project-management fees disappear; margin settles at 18%.
bear.terminal_rationale: 9x cap and 1% terminal growth reflect a sub-scale China property manager with a captive-client franchise that has stopped growing.

scenario_narratives.base: The post-spinoff platform stabilises at roughly its current size. FY2026 revenue falls ~7% (H1 -5.7%, with the H1 industrial-park factory deliveries not repeating in H2 and project-management fees still tracking the controlling shareholder's smaller private development book), dips again in FY2027, then grows ~2.5-3% from FY2028 as property management (46% of revenue, ~84m sqm under management) and asset operation (maturing malls, light-asset parks) outweigh the decline of project management and a small, break-even real-estate technology unit. The EBITDA margin eases from an underlying 24% to 22.5% as the high-margin connected-party project fees shrink within the mix. Cash tax 31%, net cash and RMB406m of wealth-management products added, RMB273m of lease liabilities and RMB134m of NCI deducted. The axes are: how far the captive project-management stream falls, whether third-party and non-residential mandates replace it, and whether the asset-operation portfolio keeps lifting NOI.
scenario_narratives.bull: The light-asset pivot works. Third-party project-management mandates (Wuxi, Xuzhou) and non-residential property management (hospitals, elderly care, industrial parks) replace the shrinking connected-party pipeline from FY2027, asset operation scales with new parks and the matured flagship mall, and REMAC ASPACE's Hong Kong modular-construction certification turns the technology segment to breakeven. Revenue returns to 5-6% growth in FY2028-30 and the margin reaches 25.5%. A 14x cap and 2.5% terminal growth still assume no re-rating beyond a mid-tier property-services multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The listed vehicle is a captive service arm whose client is shrinking. The controlling family's private developer keeps cutting launches, so project-management revenue falls ~40% a year to a residual, the connected-transaction agreements are renewed on worse terms after Dec 2026, real-estate technology is wound down, and H1 2026's factory deliveries prove to be a one-off. Revenue bottoms ~28% below FY2025 at an 18% EBITDA margin (property management and rental only) and grows 1% thereafter; the near-100% dividend payout becomes unsustainable and is cut. Terminal value capped at 9x with 1% growth. No scenario hits the zero-TV floor: the property-management base is profitable on its own.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (two clean years of history), a single dominant connected client whose own pipeline is shrinking (project management -35% YoY in H1 2026), framework agreements that expire in Dec 2026, and a China property cycle management itself calls 'L-shaped'. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (third-party wins, asset-operation scale-up, REMAC ASPACE breakeven) in a sector where the leaders are far larger. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the business that exists after the October 2024 distribution in specie, not the developer that preceded it: a RMB4bn-revenue, 22-24% EBITDA-margin, net-cash property-services platform with ~RMB4.8bn of investment property at fair value and ~46% of revenue in recurring property-management fees. Owner FCF is built from components (margin, 2% D&A, 1% capex, 31% cash tax, working capital on the revenue change) rather than carried forward from FY2025's working-capital-flattered RMB947m reported FCF. Terminal value is capped at 9-14x FCF because sub-scale China property managers have not commanded Gordon-growth multiples. Risk is charged once, in the flows and the 30/50/20 weighting, at an 11% CNY discount rate. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at the dated fx_rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Connected-party dependence: project-management and construction-materials revenue flows from the controlling shareholder's private developer under framework agreements that expire December 2026; the H1 2026 -35% in that segment is the single largest driver of the bear case
Two clean years of history: FY2024 continuing and FY2025 are the only annual observations of the post-spinoff cost base and margin, and H1 2026 already softened (-5.7% revenue, -16.7% profit)
Lumpy asset-operation revenue: RMB314m of H1 2026 revenue was industrial-park factory deliveries recognised at a point in time; the base and bear cases assume they do not recur at that scale
Real-estate technology (REMAC ASPACE) lost RMB110m in FY2025 and RMB48m in H1 2026; the base case assumes losses narrow, not that the unit becomes a growth engine

Near-100% dividend payout on a cash pile that fell from RMB1,601m to RMB1,119m in six months (partly RMB582m of net borrowing repayment and RMB187m into wealth-management products); a payout cut would not change intrinsic value but would likely hit the price

Investment properties (RMB4.8bn, fair-value model) sit inside the operating flows via asset-operation rental; a sharper China commercial-property downturn would hit both the rental line and the deferred-tax-protected book value
Currency: CNY flows against an HKD quote; the fx_rate is dated and is not refreshed by price-only updates

Discount-rate judgment: an 11% CNY WACC values even the bear case above the market price, i.e. the market is applying a much higher implied cost of equity (trailing P/E ~4.8x) for governance and China-property risk than this model charges
